source_evidence: Most smart investors put enough money in savings to cover an emergency, like sudden unemployment. Savings are usually put into safe places that allow you access to your money at any time.
question: Misconception: Savings accounts earn little interest, so they have no place in an emergency fund.
answer: A low interest rate does not make savings useless for emergencies. The source describes savings as a way to keep money accessible and says people put enough in savings to cover an emergency. It also notes that some people invest money to seek more growth over longer periods.
